capabilities.test: Top-level index organizes the curriculum into an explicit progression with prerequisites or paths
At least one lesson ships runnable code in more than one programming language
Curriculum covers LLM application engineering, RAG, and agents
Curriculum has dedicated MCP lessons or projects
Core algorithms are implemented from first principles and then mapped to production libraries
Learners can run meaningful lesson code without local setup via browser execution, Colab, or Codespaces
Learners can identify a starting level or personalized path
Every lesson that claims a shipped artifact has a non-empty outputs directory with the artifact
Curriculum has a public web-rendered learning surface
Every lesson has a valid formative assessment and useful answer feedback
Every lesson satisfies the documented objectives, language, prerequisite, pedagogy, code, test, quiz, and artifact contract
All documented repository audits, content checks, count checks, and site tests exit zero on the current worktree
A clean checkout has a documented, pinned environment and canonical command that runs representative lessons across supported languages
Time-sensitive or quantitative technical claims link to primary sources and pass an automated citation gate
Learners can see persisted progress across lessons and learning paths
CI executes lesson code, notebooks, and site behavior on every relevant pull request
A supported install command exposes reusable curriculum code as a package
A root setup guide covers supported runtimes, dependency installation, API keys, and troubleshooting
Guided exercises have hidden or separate reference solutions and verification tests
At least one complete non-English content track is maintained alongside localized UI
Key modules include short guided demonstrations or equivalent narrated walkthroughs
